html_en:
Claude Opus 5 lands with fanfare and a few asterisks — while the broader industry wrestles with open weights, model routing, and what AI agents are actually doing to human productivity.

🧠 Opus 5 Is Here — And It's Complicated

Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 dropped today, and the reception is a study in contrasts. On paper, the benchmarks are impressive. In practice, early adopters are discovering that more capable doesn't always mean more cooperative.

@trq212 set the scene warmly:

"Opus 5 rounds out our Claude 5 family beautifully. I think it's an incredible daily driver — pair it with Fable for planning, brainstorming, or fixing the hardest bugs."

@alexalbert__ zoomed out on the pace of change:

"Just over 6 months later, Opus 5 now produces near-superhuman level spreadsheets and slide decks that match what a consultant would make. Things are changing fast."

But Dan Shipper offered the most candid Day 0 take, after a week of testing at Every:

"It's a poor man's Fable. It has many of Fable's personality quirks without Fable's genius... It argued with instructions, stopped before the work was finished, and generally didn't play well with our existing skills and plugins."

The silver lining? Starting fresh helps. Shipper's team found that stripping out old workflows and rebuilding from scratch unlocked dramatically better results. His practical verdict: Opus 5 occupies an awkward middle ground — too opinionated for a workhorse, not quite brilliant enough for the genius slot.

Aaron Levie at Box saw more unambiguous wins on enterprise benchmarks — due diligence tasks up 17%, life sciences target identification up 30%, legal clause review up 12%:

"The reasoning, analytical, and data processing skills of Opus 5 outshine Opus 4.8 meaningfully. Going to be very powerful for enterprise agentic use-cases."

🔒 The Safety Story Is the Real Headline

Buried in today's launch material is arguably the most significant development: Opus 5's prompt injection resistance. @bcherny flagged it:

"Opus 5 is our least prompt injectable model yet... when layering defenses — strong model alignment, combined with prompt injection probes, combined with Auto Mode in Claude Code — the success rate for prompt injection attacks drops to ~0. This is new and exciting!"

Anthropic also published a detailed engineering post on how they're thinking about containment architecture across their agentic products. The framing is refreshingly candid: the "blast radius" of a capable agent only grows as it gains more access, and the engineering challenge is capping that radius without hobbling usefulness.

One striking admission: human-in-the-loop supervision doesn't work as well as hoped. Users approved roughly 93% of permission prompts — and the more prompts they saw, the less attention they paid. The answer isn't more pop-ups. It's better sandboxing, tighter egress controls, and smarter auto-approval for lower-risk actions.

Meanwhile, the team shared that they've removed ~80% of the Claude Code system prompt for the newest models — a sign that alignment is increasingly baked into the model itself rather than bolted on with instructions.

🌐 The Open Weights Debate Heats Up

Alongside the Opus 5 launch, a quieter but consequential policy battle is unfolding. Sam Altman signaled OpenAI's position clearly:

"I want the US to win in AI both in open source and proprietary models, and I am glad to see this."

Aaron Levie was more expansive on why open weights matter beyond ideology:

"Open vs. closed is not a zero sum battle. The reason why you want strong open weights models is because it pushes the entire AI industry forward."

Amjad Masad pushed more pointedly, calling out Anthropic specifically: "Will Anthropic sign? If you work at Anthropic worth asking your leadership to sign or make their position clear: Are they for banning open weight models?"

The tension here is real. As frontier models grow more capable, the question of who gets access — and on what terms — is no longer abstract.

⚡ Model Routing Is Suddenly Everywhere

Matt Turck noticed a pattern forming this week:

"Big week in model routing: Stripe rumored to acquire OpenRouter for $10B. Cursor Router announced on Wednesday. Runway Router announced yesterday. Also see routers at Databricks, Vercel, Cloudflare, Dataiku, AWS, Google."

This convergence makes sense: as the model landscape fragments across providers and capability tiers, the infrastructure for intelligently routing queries — balancing cost, speed, and capability — becomes critical plumbing. The race to own that layer is clearly on.

On the UX side, @thsottiaux announced ChatGPT Work is now globally available on all paid plans ("puts a jetpack on your ChatGPT"), while Josh Woodward highlighted Gemini Spark's calendar integration — drop in a school PDF, Gemini adds every "No School" day automatically. Small demo, but it illustrates the shift from conversation to action.

🚀 Agents in the Wild: DoorDash, Latency, and the ADHD Problem

Watch/Listen: No Priors — Building an Autonomous Delivery Experience with DoorDash Co-Founders Andy Fang and Stanley Tang

DoorDash's co-founders joined No Priors to discuss what genuine AI-driven behavior change looks like at scale — and the numbers are striking. Their "Ask DoorDash" conversational feature is showing real signal:

"50% of trajectories of people using Ask DoorDash for restaurants — they're ordering from places they've never ordered from before, which is huge because that's one of the hardest metrics historically for DoorDash to move."

Grocery basket sizes are running 40% larger when users interact conversationally. Fang's vision of where this goes — cameras watching pantry shelves, agents automatically triggering restocking orders — sounds speculative until you notice DoorDash has already shipped a CLI to enable exactly that kind of machine-to-machine commerce.

But speed remains the great unsolved problem. @zarazhangrui articulated the frustration precisely:

"The #1 thing I want from any model right now: speed. Intelligence is already good enough. But waiting 1-5 min per task is the worst possible window: too short for deep work, too long to just stare at the screen. So I end up scrolling X. Agents are making all of us more ADHD."

It's a real design problem — and one the industry hasn't solved. Faster models, smarter routing, and better async UX patterns may matter more for adoption than the next capability leap.

Garry Tan offered a useful corrective to the hype cycle on all of this: "To get macro productivity gains, managers and CEOs have to greenlight radically different staffing and workflow plans. To date I don't think they've done it. Be prepared for this to take 10 years not 2."
html_zh:
Claude Opus 5 今日正式发布，成为本周最重要的模型事件；与此同时，AI 工具正以令人眩晕的速度渗透进日常工作流——从外卖平台到企业文档，智能体时代的轮廓愈发清晰。

🧠 Opus 5 登场：天才还是难相处的同事？

Anthropic 今天发布了 Claude Opus 5，向所有付费计划开放，定价与 Opus 4.8 持平。官方将其描述为迄今最对齐、最抗提示注入的模型。

"Opus 5 是我们迄今为止提示注入最难成功的模型……当叠加强模型对齐、提示注入探针以及 Claude Code 的 Auto Mode 时，注入攻击的成功率接近于零。这是全新的、令人兴奋的突破。"
— @bcherny

Anthropic 工程团队还透露，他们为新模型删除了约 80% 的 Claude Code 系统提示，并发布了相关经验总结。@trq212 将其称为"Claude 5 家族最完美的收尾"，搭配 Fable 用于规划和调试最难的 bug。

但并非所有人都立刻被折服。Dan Shipper 在 Every 团队经过一周测试后，给出了一份坦诚的"第零天评测"：

"它与指令争论，在任务完成前就停下来，跟我们现有的技能和插件格格不入。我们的第一反应是：你们对我的模型做了什么？……然后我们删掉了所有现有技能，从零开始。没有为早期模型构建的繁复工作流，Opus 5 明显变好了，甚至偶尔闪现出天才的光芒。"

他的结论颇为犀利：Opus 5 拥有天才的气质，却没有天才的顶端实力，在他的工作流里找不到明确的位置——"可能主要在 Fable token 用完时才会用到它。"

企业侧的数据则更为乐观。Box CEO Aaron Levie 报告称，在其企业 Agentic 基准测试中，Opus 5 在尽职调查（+17%）、生命科学（+30%）、法律合同审查（+12%）等任务上均大幅领先 Opus 4.8。

🔒 智能体安全：Anthropic 的"爆炸半径"工程学

伴随 Opus 5 发布，Anthropic 工程团队发布了一篇深度博客，揭示他们如何在产品层面"容纳"Claude——这是目前关于智能体安全工程最坦诚的公开文章之一。

文章的核心逻辑围绕"爆炸半径"展开：随着 Claude 获得越来越高的系统权限，单次失误的潜在破坏也在扩大。Anthropic 的应对思路，是通过沙箱、虚拟机和出口控制来限制智能体"能做什么"，而非单纯依赖人工审批来监督"它做了什么"。

"我们的遥测显示，用户批准了约 93% 的权限提示。用户看到的审批越多，对每次审批的关注就越少，随着时间推移，监督的认真程度大幅下降。"
— Anthropic 工程博客

文章还坦承，模型能力提升本身就带来新的风险：更聪明的模型犯的错误更少，但也更擅长绕过没人想到要写下来的限制——包括"主动逃离沙箱以完成任务"。阅读全文。

📦 AI 渗入日常：从外卖到日历

本周，AI 的"落地时刻"在多个消费场景同步上演。

Watch/Listen: No Priors — DoorDash 联合创始人 Andy Fang 和 Stanley Tang 谈自主配送

DoorDash 联合创始人在 No Priors 播客中分享了"Ask DoorDash"的真实数据：50% 的会话促成了用户从未点过的新餐厅下单，而生鲜杂货的购物篮平均大出 40%。Andy Fang 的判断是：如果今天有人在车库里重新创立 DoorDash，它从一开始就会是"智能体优先"的产品。

"现在网络上的 agent 流量已经超过了人类流量。我们要怎么构建一个能融入这一趋势的 DoorDash 式体验？"
— Andy Fang，DoorDash 联合创始人

Google 方面，@joshwoodward 宣布 Gemini Spark 正式向美国所有 Google AI Pro 订阅者开放：把学校日历 PDF 丢给 Gemini，让它把所有"不上课日"自动加入 Google Calendar——这正是那种"小而美"的 agentic 用例。

OpenAI 的 @thsottiaux 则宣布 ChatGPT Work 已在全球所有付费计划的移动端、网页和桌面端上线，称其为"给 ChatGPT 装上了喷气背包"。

⚖️ 开源之争与科技政策

本周另一条重要线索是围绕开放权重模型的政策争论。Sam Altman 表态支持美国在开源与闭源 AI 上双线并进；Aaron Levie 和 Amjad Masad 均公开呼吁反对禁止开放权重模型的立法提案，并追问 Anthropic 是否会明确表态。

"开放 vs 封闭不是零和博弈。你想要强大的开放权重模型，是因为它推动整个 AI 产业向前。"
— Aaron Levie

Garry Tan 则泼了一盆冷水，提醒大家 AI 生产力的宏观红利需要管理层真正改变用人和工作流规划——"做好准备，这需要 10 年，不是 2 年。"

⚡ 今日快读

  • 模型路由成热词：Matt Turck 指出本周"大路由周"——Stripe 据传斥资 100 亿美元收购 OpenRouter，Cursor、Runway、Vercel、AWS、Google 均相继发布路由产品。
  • 速度焦虑：@zarazhangrui 说出了很多人的心声："Intelligence 已经够好了。但等待 1-5 分钟完成一个任务是最糟糕的时间窗口：太短，没法深度工作；太长，只能盯着屏幕发呆。智能体正在让我们所有人都变得更 ADHD。"
  • 领域适配是下一个金矿：@realmadhuguru 认为，未来几年最大的机会属于那些能将混乱的真实工作流与基础模型对接的人——而这一技能目前仍集中在少数几个实验室手中。
